# v3.32.0

Covers everything since **v3.31.0**.

This release adds **maps** to the offering dashboard, so you can see where your delivery capability actually sits rather than reading it out of a table. It also corrects **two figures that were being reported wrongly**, and rebuilds the PDF exports for Compliance Planning and the program dashboards so a printed copy looks like the page it came from.

Unlike the last release, this one **does change stored data and the database schema** — see *For administrators* at the end. Nothing needs doing by hand, but it is worth reading before you update.

## New — delivery geography on a map

The offering dashboard now draws a world map above the specialisation tables, with two views:

- **Delivery geography** (the default) shades every country as **Onshore**, **Nearshore** or **Rest of world** for the scope you have selected.
- **Holder density** shades countries by how many people hold one particular required training, chosen from a dropdown.

Three things about it are worth knowing, because they are deliberate:

- **The map is an addition, never a replacement.** The tables stay exactly where they were, directly beneath it.
- **It shows distribution, not compliance.** A requirement is met across your onshore countries *as a whole*, so people spread across three countries can satisfy a requirement that no single country meets on its own. The map is therefore coloured in neutral hues rather than the green/amber/red used elsewhere, so it is never mistaken for a per-country pass or fail.
- **The density view is drawn per requirement, not per offering.** That is what lets you check it: adding up a requirement's countries reproduces the figure shown in its row. There is deliberately no whole-offering version, because one person holding two of an offering's trainings is still one person, so such a map would not add up to anything on screen.

The maps are included in PDF exports of the dashboard.

## New — ISO country codes in Region Data

Placing a country on a map means matching your country name to a real country, and names do not match reliably — "UK" and "United Kingdom" are the same place and no automatic comparison will say so. Left alone, that kind of mismatch fails *silently*: the country is quietly left off and the total is under-reported.

Region Data therefore now carries an **ISO country code** column, which you can search, sort, filter, import and export like any other.

- **A missing code is reported, never guessed.** The Region Data page shows a standing amber count of countries without one, and any map lists the countries it could not place rather than dropping them.
- **"Suggest ISO codes"** opens a review queue that matches only the countries currently without a code, shows you the name each one matched against, and applies **nothing** until you tick it. Nothing is pre-ticked. An automatic name match would just be a new way to be silently wrong, which is the problem the column exists to remove.
- **Two countries may share a code.** A sales geography that lists sub-national entries separately is a real arrangement, so the column does not force uniqueness; anything reading it adds those rows together.

## Fixed — two figures that were wrong

- **Compliance Planning counted some people more than once.** Where a single certification was required by several specialisations, the "People to certify" headline charged for it once *per specialisation*, so a certification needed by three specialisations reported three times the people it actually takes. It is now counted once. Each specialisation block still shows what it would cost on its own, and where those blocks add up to more than the headline, the requirement now carries a "shared with…" note and a short line explaining why the two figures differ.

- **A country with no region defined displayed the word "Unknown".** When an import met a country that was not yet in Region Data it recorded the region as the literal text `Unknown` — which was only ever meant as "not known yet", but nothing downstream could tell the difference, so it was shown as though it were the name of a region: in the Region Data table, in every geography filter, on the student record, in the Region column of every report, and in every export. Those now show an empty cell, and the geography filters no longer offer a region that does not exist.

## Changed — PDF exports that look like the page

The **Compliance Planning** and **program compliance dashboard** PDFs have been rebuilt.

They previously flattened everything into one very wide table — the planning roadmap ran to eighteen columns, which left most cells wrapping to one word per line and a header row broken mid-word. Colour did not survive at all, and the metric cards at the top of the page came out as a plain two-column list.

The PDF now mirrors the page: the coloured metric cards, a card per specialisation with its badges and notes, the same red/amber/green shading, figures kept together in one cell as they read on screen (`4 → 2 / 4` with its expiring note beneath), and each person's reasons printed under their row. A section with nothing in it prints the explanation rather than an empty header row. On the program dashboards, the tier ladder and the per-theatre breakdowns now reach the PDF — previously neither did.

**CSV and Excel exports are unchanged**, byte for byte. They remain the wide machine-readable tables, with every column present, for anyone who pivots or scripts against them.

Two smaller export fixes ride along: a renewal now prints in a different colour from a lapse, matching how the page distinguishes them; and check marks and similar symbols no longer come out as mojibake in a PDF.

## For administrators

**There are two database migrations in this release, and one of them changes existing data.** Both run automatically as part of the update.

1. A new, optional **ISO code** column is added to Region Data. Existing rows get no code, which is a valid state — nothing breaks, and the maps simply report those countries as unplaced until you fill them in.
2. Any Region Data row whose region is the placeholder word **`Unknown`** is changed to an **empty** region. The match ignores case and surrounding spaces, because that value also arrived through imports and manual edits over the years. This is the fix described above; if you have a country genuinely *named* Unknown, it would be caught by this, which is worth a glance at the Region Data page after updating.

**To get the most out of the maps**, visit Region Data after updating and use **Suggest ISO codes** to fill in the countries you recognise. The amber count tells you how many are still unplaced. Nothing else on the page depends on it — reports, filters and every existing figure work exactly as before without a single code set.

The map outlines are a small file the browser fetches when a map is first shown, so they add nothing to the size of the rest of the application.
